title: Jet Pump / Eductor

introduction.definition: A jet pump (eductor or ejector) has no moving parts. A motive fluid under pressure accelerates through a converging nozzle into a high-velocity jet; the low static pressure and momentum of the jet entrain the suction fluid, the two streams mix in the throat, and the diffuser converts velocity back into pressure.
applications: Priming centrifugal pumps and vacuum duties
Deep-well jet pumps for domestic water
key_points: No moving parts — robust and simple
Performance set by area ratio and flow ratio
introduction.summary: A jet pump has no moving parts. A motive fluid (water, steam or air) under pressure accelerates through a converging nozzle into a high-velocity jet. The jet's low static pressure and its momentum drag the surrounding suction fluid into the mixing throat, where the two streams exchange momentum and mix; the diffuser then slows the mixture and converts velocity back into pressure. Efficiency is modest, but the device is simple, robust, self-priming and handles slurries, corrosives and gases.

video_tutorials.title: Jet Pump / Eductor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Jet Pump / Eductor.
A jet pump (eductor or ejector) has no moving parts.

A motive fluid under pressure accelerates through a converging nozzle into a high-velocity jet; the low static pressure and momentum of the jet entrain the suction fluid, the two streams mix in the throat, and the diffuser converts velocity back into pressure.
Typical applications include tank mixing and sludge suspension; priming centrifugal pumps and vacuum duties; deep-well jet pumps for domestic water; chemical induction and dewatering.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Eductor Body (Suction Chamber, Throat, Diffuser).

video_tutorials.title: Jet Pump / Eductor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Jet Pump / Eductor.
Monitor motive and suction pressure.
Measure nozzle bore wear.
Inspect throat for erosion.
Watch for nozzle wear: higher motive flow, lower suction. Common cause: erosion.
Watch for blockage: no suction. Common cause: debris in nozzle.
Watch for back-flow into suction: motive fluid exits suction. Common cause: discharge blocked.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
